belief: I have nothing left to give.
origins: Long illness, caregiving, or chronic fatigue can leave us depleted. With no energy to give, we may feel empty and ashamed.
teaches: Peter said to the lame man, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you.” We always have something. Jesus said, “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” You may need to receive before you give. “Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you.” Rest is not failure. In due time you will have more to share, and meanwhile your presence, prayers, and gratitude bless others.
self_statements: Everyone gives more than I do.
errors: Believing I am either giving fully or giving nothing.
Predicting that I will always be empty.
Feeling depleted and concluding that I have nothing.
questions: What do I still have: time, prayers, listening, thanks?
Whom could I bless in a small way?
What do I need to receive first?
Who might want to give to me?
What does Scripture say about rest and strength?
What is one small thing I can give?
truth: I may be depleted, but I am not empty-handed. I can receive rest and care from God and others, and give small things as strength allows. My presence and prayers matter.
hw_truths: Jesus gives rest to the weary.
He gives power to the faint.
Receiving is part of the cycle.
log: Each week, note one thing you received and one you gave.
prayer: Lord, I am empty. Restore me, give me strength, and let me give what I can. Amen.
